title: Her stepfather Fletcher Burley, gambler and protector
summary: Fletcher Burley loved her, was generous and feared in Pittsburgh, and took her into gambling joints under a big coat to play. Mayfield again rescued her from stranded tours.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What sort of a man was he?

He was the kind of a man that he loved me so much he would almost put his own kids aside for me, if I needed anything. Well, he was very charitable. Sometimes I'd bring kids in that didn't have shoes and he'd give them money to buy shoes or to buy clothing. Fletcher had a big coat - this is funny - he had a big oversized coat made and he took me in gambling joints and everywhere and he'd put me under this coat because.... (NOT CLEAR) He was considered a very good, bad man, not overbearing but he was treacherous if you made him angry. Everybody in Pittsburgh knew about this and nobody even tried to harm me. But he was a very sweet man. He'd say, "Stop the game. I want you to hear my little girl play." He'd put a dollar in the hat and then they'd pass the hat around after I had finished and he'd take me outside and he'd say, "Give me my dollar back."... My mother didn't know what he was doing until three years ago. I was talking to her and she said 'My Goodness, you didn't tell me!'
Just a few. They were big influences people of course in music.
Yes, he was, but he was a strange man. He would

not gamble. He worked every day; he would not gamble with that money. He'd take the money home and give it to my mother for her bills and what-not and he'd go up the street and have a friend throw him in the game. That's what they called it - that is, give him a stake in the game. He was a terrific gambler.
Now you talked about Roland Mayfield coming out and getting you when you were stranded. Were you touring the whole time -

I was with home talent shows and things like that. I was talking to him one time, "Roland, do you remember when you picked me up in New York when I was stranded?" He said, "New York, Buffalo, Cincinnati, Chicago, Cleveland, Steubenville."
